# Trans-Java EV Road Trip: Jakarta to Yogyakarta — Indonesia's First EV Highway

Indonesia's Trans-Java Toll Road is the backbone of the nation's EV transition — a continuous expressway stretching nearly 1,000 km across the most populous island on Earth. The stretch from Jakarta to Yogyakarta (~540 km) is the crown jewel: a route that takes you from the hyper-modern capital, through volcanic highlands, past ancient temples, and into the cultural heart of Java.

For families considering an EV road trip in Asia, this is the Indonesian route to beat in 2026. The charging infrastructure has matured rapidly — PLN SPKLU stations now dot the rest areas at regular intervals, private operators like Electrum and Charge+ have added high-speed 150 kW chargers, and hotels in every major stopover city offer overnight AC charging.

This guide covers everything: the exact charging stations along the route with real 2026 data, family-friendly stops from Bandung's cool highlands to Yogyakarta's ancient temples, EV-friendly hotels, a full cost breakdown for a family of 4, and the practical tips you need to drive this route with confidence.

## Why the Trans-Java is Indonesia's First Real EV Highway

In 2024, the Jakarta-Yogyakarta EV corridor was still experimental — you needed patience, a backup plan, and nerves of steel. By 2026, it's a completely different story.

### What Changed

- **PLN installed 50-100 kW DC chargers at every major rest area** between Jakarta and Yogyakarta, spaced roughly 50-80 km apart
- **Electrum and Charge+ added 120-150 kW ultra-fast chargers** at strategic locations (KM 228 Cirebon, KM 391 Kendal, KM 486 Salatiga)
- **Hotel charging became standard** — nearly every mid-range hotel in Bandung, Semarang, and Yogyakarta now offers at least a 7-22 kW AC charger
- **PLN Mobile app matured** — real-time charger availability, QRIS payment, and user-reported status have made broken-charger anxiety a thing of the past

The result? Jakarta to Yogyakarta is now Indonesia's most practical long-distance EV route — and one of the most scenic road trips in all of Southeast Asia.

## Suggested 4-Day Family Itinerary

### Day 1: Jakarta → Bandung Detour (~200 km, 4-5 hours)

**Morning: Depart Jakarta (6:00 AM)**

Top up to 95%+ the night before at **Kota Kasablanka** (100 kW DC, 4 slots) or your hotel. Leave early to beat Jakarta's legendary traffic. By 6:30 AM you should be on the Jakarta-Cikampek Toll Road heading east.

**Stop: Rest Area KM 52A (Cikampek)**

First stretch is 65 km of stop-and-go traffic. Your battery might actually hold steady thanks to regenerative braking. If you need a quick top-up, KM 52A has a 50 kW PLN charger. Otherwise, push through to Bandung.

**Detour Option: Cipularang Toll Road to Bandung (~11:00 AM)**

Instead of heading straight for Cirebon, consider a rewarding detour south on the Cipularang Toll Road to Bandung (150 km from Jakarta, 1.5 hours from the Cikampek junction).

Bandung — the "Paris of Java" — sits at 768m elevation in a cool mountain basin. The climb is steep (7m to 768m in 60 km of driving), so expect 25-35% higher energy consumption. The descent on the way back will regenerate 10-15%.

**Family Activity: Gedung Sate**

Bandung's iconic colonial building (completed 1924) with a distinctive skewer-topped central tower. The grounds have a lovely park where kids can run around. Free entry to the outside grounds; the museum inside is Rp 15,000 entry.

**Family Activity: Tangkuban Perahu Volcano (30 km north of Bandung)**

An active volcano with a drive-to-the-rim crater at 2,084m. The road climbs another 1,300m from Bandung — expect 15-20°C temperatures even at midday.

- **Cost:** Rp 200,000 adult, Rp 100,000 child (includes guide)
- **Duration:** 2-3 hours
- **Kid tip:** The crater path is paved and stroller-friendly. The sulfur smell is strong — bring masks (sold at entrance).
- **EV note:** The climb uses 25-30% battery, but the descent regenerates most of it. Start with 50%+ charge.

**Lunch: Floating Market Lembang**

A lakeside market where you eat from boats. Pedal swan boats, mini train rides, and a rabbit park keep kids entertained for hours. Rp 30,000 entry.

**Charging in Bandung:** Trans Studio Mall (PLN SPKLU DC 100 kW, 4 slots) or your hotel.

**EV-Friendly Hotel in Bandung:** {{BOOKING}} for Sheraton Bandung Hotel & Towers — AC 22 kW charging, pool, central location on Jalan Sudirman. Or {{KLOOK}} for Bandung hotel deals.

---

### Day 2: Bandung → Semarang (~350 km via Cirebon, 6-7 hours)

**Morning: Descend from Bandung (8:00 AM)**

Leave Bandung with 80%+ battery. The descent back to the Trans-Java mainline regenerates 10-15% — you'll gain back more than you expect.

**Charging Stop: KM 228A Cirebon (Electrum 120 kW)**

Charge to 80% while the family explores Cirebon's batik workshops. **Batik Trusmi Village** (15 minutes from the rest area) lets kids try batik-making for Rp 100,000-150,000.

**Lunch Stop: KM 260B Tegal rest area**

A 50 kW PLN charger here if you need a top-up. The food court has solid Indonesian options — try nasi lengko (rice with tofu, bean sprouts, and peanut sauce).

**Afternoon: Arrive Semarang (~4:00 PM)**

Semarang, the capital of Central Java, is your stopover for the night. The approach from the west involves a winding descent through mountain tunnels — regenerative heaven.

**Family Activity: Sam Poo Kong**

Indonesia's largest Chinese temple complex, built in the 15th century by Admiral Zheng He's fleet. The architecture is stunning — red and gold pagodas, dragon statues, incense-heavy courtyards. Free entry.

**Family Activity: Semarang Old Town (Kota Lama)**

A district of beautifully preserved Dutch Art Deco buildings, cobblestone streets, and trendy cafes. The **Lawang Sewu** building ("Building of a Thousand Doors") is a must-visit for its spooky corridors and hidden staircases. Rp 20,000 adult, Rp 10,000 child.

**Charging in Semarang:**

| Station | Location | Speed | Slots |
|---------|----------|-------|-------|
| PLN SPKLU Paragon Mall | City Center | 100 kW | 4 |
| Electrum Semarang | Near Tugu Muda | 120 kW | 4 |

**EV-Friendly Hotel in Semarang:** {{BOOKING}} for Holiday Inn Semarang — AC 22 kW charging, rooftop pool with great city views, central location near Paragon Mall.

---

### Day 3: Semarang → Yogyakarta via Solo (~120 km, 2-3 hours)

**Morning: Depart Semarang (9:00 AM)**

Short drive today — just 120 km to Yogyakarta. But it's one of the most scenic stretches of the entire Trans-Java, winding through the Salatiga highlands with views of Mount Merbabu and (on clear days) the smoking peak of Mount Merapi.

**Charging Stop: KM 486A Salatiga (Charge+ 150 kW)**

Even if you don't need a full charge, stop here. This is the best rest area on the entire route — ultra-fast 150 kW chargers, a modern food court, clean family restrooms, and a small playground for kids. Charge from 50% to 80% in just 12 minutes.

**Optional Stop: Solo (Surakarta)**

Solo is Yogyakarta's quieter twin — a traditional Javanese court city without the tourist crowds. Worth a 2-hour stop if you have time:

- **Keraton Surakarta** — The official palace of the Surakarta Sultanate. Rp 25,000 entry.
- **Pasar Klewer** — Legendary batik market. Bargain hard.
- **Serabi Notosuman** — Solo's famous pancake-like snack. Rp 5,000 each.

**Afternoon: Arrive Yogyakarta (~1:00 PM)**

Rolling into Yogyakarta from the north is a magical experience. The road passes through rice paddies, past the silhouette of Mount Merapi, and ends in the bustling, artistic chaos of Java's cultural soul.

**Charging on Arrival:** Hartono Mall (100 kW, 4 slots) or Jogja City Mall (100 kW, 4 slots).

**Afternoon Activity: Malioboro Street**

The legendary shopping street at Yogyakarta's heart. Two kilometers of batik shops, street food stalls, becak (rickshaw) drivers, and street musicians. The pedestrian section in the evenings is a carnival atmosphere.

**Kid tip:** Try wedang ronde (ginger drink with glutinous rice balls) from the street vendors — Rp 10,000 per cup. The becak rides to the palace cost Rp 30,000-50,000.

**Sunset: Tugu Yogyakarta**

The iconic white monument at the intersection of Jalan Margo Utomo and Jalan A.M. Sangaji. Best photographed at golden hour with the horse carts passing by.

**EV-Friendly Hotel in Yogyakarta:** {{BOOKING}} for Tentrem Hotel Yogyakarta — AC 22 kW charging, excellent pool, family suites, and a central location near Malioboro. {{KLOOK}} for Yogyakarta hotel deals.

---

### Day 4: Yogyakarta — Temples & Culture

**Sunrise: Borobudur Temple (6:00 AM)**

The world's largest Buddhist temple — a 9th-century monument of 2,672 relief panels and 504 Buddha statues. Arrive at 5:30 AM for the sunrise ticket (Rp 375,000 adult, Rp 225,000 child — includes access to the upper levels). Watching the sun rise over the Kedu Plain from the upper terraces is genuinely one of the most moving experiences in Asia.

- **Distance from Yogyakarta:** 40 km northwest (50 min drive)
- **EV note:** Parking has some regular AC outlets (7 kW) — no DC fast charging yet. Start with 60%+ battery for the round trip.
- **Kid tip:** The walk up is steep in places. Carry small kids. There are shaded rest areas at each level.

{{KLOOK}} for Borobudur sunrise tickets

**Mid-Morning: Prambanan Temple (10:00 AM)**

A 9th-century Hindu temple complex dedicated to Trimurti — Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. The main temple stands 47m tall. The Ramayana ballet performances (evenings) are spectacular.

- **Distance from Borobudur:** 50 km southeast (1 hour drive)
- **Cost:** Rp 50,000 adult, Rp 25,000 child
- **Kid tip:** The park is large and flat — good for strollers. Deer roam freely in the grounds.

**Lunch: Gudeg at Malioboro**

Yogyakarta's signature dish — young jackfruit cooked in coconut milk and palm sugar, served with rice, chicken, and hard-boiled egg. Try **Gudeg Yu Djum** (Jalan Wijilan) — the most famous version since 1951. Rp 30,000-50,000 per portion.

**Afternoon: Water Palace (Taman Sari) & Kraton**

- **Kraton Ngayogyakarta Hadiningrat** — The Sultan's palace, still a functioning royal residence. Traditional Javanese architecture, gamelan performances, and silent batik makers. Rp 40,000 entry.
- **Taman Sari (Water Castle)** — A 18th-century pleasure garden with bathing pools, underground tunnels, and a ruined fortress. Kids love the maze-like passages. Rp 25,000 entry.

**Evening: Alun-Alun Kidul Night Market**

The southern square transforms into a massive night market every evening. The highlight: driving a "odon-odon" (decorated pedal car) through a row of giant banyan trees. Blindfolded drivers who walk between the trees will have their wishes fulfilled — according to local legend. Rp 30,000 per car.

## Practical Tips for Families Driving the Trans-Java in an EV

### Tol-List (Electronic Toll) Setup

Indonesia's toll roads use contactless electronic toll collection. Make sure you have one of these before departure:

1. **e-Toll Card** — Buy at any Indomaret or Alfamart. Top up at the counter or via mobile banking. Rp 30,000 card fee, then load with Rp 500,000+ for the trip.
2. **Flazz (BCA)** — Works on all toll roads. Top up via BCA mobile.
3. **Mandiri e-Money** — Mandiri bank card, widely accepted.

**Pro tip:** Keep at least Rp 150,000 balance on your toll card. Running out mid-trip means a long queue at the top-up booth.

### Charging App Registration (Do This BEFORE You Leave)

**PLN Mobile:**
1. Download from Google Play Store or Apple App Store
2. Register with your phone number (Indonesian SIM recommended)
3. Create a profile (name, email)
4. Top up your balance (minimum Rp 50,000 via GoPay, OVO, or bank transfer)
5. Now you can scan the QR code at any SPKLU charger to start charging

**Charge+:**
1. Download and register with email or Google account
2. Add a payment method (credit card or GoPay)
3. The app will show all Charge+ stations and real-time availability

**Electrum:**
1. Similar registration process
2. Uses wallet-based payment — top up minimum Rp 50,000

### What to Pack

- [ ] **CCS2 DC charging cable** — most fast chargers have tethered cables, but some older stations don't
- [ ] **Type 2 AC cable** — essential for hotel and mall charging
- [ ] **Portable emergency charger** with Indonesian Type C/F plug adapter
- [ ] **e-Toll card** with minimum Rp 500,000 balance
- [ ] **Indonesian SIM card** (Telkomsel has best coverage along the Trans-Java)
- [ ] **Physical credit/debit card** — some chargers don't accept QRIS yet
- [ ] **Cash** — Rp 500,000+ for roadside markets, small warungs, and parking
- [ ] **E-wallets** — GoPay, OVO, ShopeePay all set up and topped up
- [ ] **Light jackets/sweatshirts** — Bandung (16-20°C evenings) and highland areas
- [ ] **Umbrellas** — short tropical showers common even in dry season
- [ ] **Sunscreen** — higher UV at mountain elevations
- [ ] **Kids' entertainment** — tablets with downloaded shows, colouring books, snacks
- [ ] **Reusable water bottles** — stay hydrated in tropical heat
- [ ] **Motion sickness medication** — the mountain roads can be winding
- [ ] **Wet wipes and change of clothes** — standard parenting travel gear

### Traffic Timing Tips

| Situation | Best Time | Avoid |
|-----------|-----------|-------|
| Leaving Jakarta | 5:00-6:00 AM | 6:30-9:00 AM, Friday 3-7 PM |
| Crossing Cipali Toll | Midday (10 AM-2 PM) | Night (poor lighting, truck-heavy) |
| Entering Semarang | Before 4:00 PM | 5:00-7:00 PM (rush hour) |
| Solo-Yogyakarta section | Any time | Sunday evening (return traffic) |
| Driving in Yogyakarta | 9:00 AM-3:00 PM | 4:30-7:00 PM (school pickup + office rush) |
| Lebaran (Eid) | Don't drive the Trans-Java during Lebaran | Peak exodus — chargers queue for hours |

### Seasonal Considerations

| Season | Months | Conditions for EV Driving |
|--------|--------|--------------------------|
| **Dry Season** | May-October | Clear views, less rain, cooler mountain temps. Peak tourist season — book hotels early. |
| **Shoulder** | March-April, November | Good weather with occasional showers. Fewer crowds. |
| **Rainy Season** | December-February | Heavy afternoon downpours. Fog on mountain sections (Salatiga, Bawen). Cheaper hotels, but slower driving. |
| **Lebaran (Eid)** | Moves annually | AVOID if possible. Mass exodus from Jakarta, toll roads gridlocked, chargers overwhelmed. |

## The Verdict: Why This is Asia's Best Emerging EV Road Trip

The Jakarta to Yogyakarta Trans-Java EV route in 2026 is a genuinely practical family road trip. The charging infrastructure has reached a tipping point: you no longer need to be an early-adopter with nerves of steel. PLN, Electrum, and Charge+ have built a corridor that works.

What makes it special isn't just the infrastructure — it's the journey itself. You climb from the tropical heat of Jakarta into the cool, volcano-ringed highlands of Bandung. You cross the fertile plains of Cirebon and Tegal. You wind through the mountain tunnels into Semarang's colonial old town. And you end in Yogyakarta — the cultural heart of Java — where Borobudur and Prambanan stand as they have for over a millennium.

For families, the EV advantage is real: the forced 20-minute charging breaks are perfectly timed for bathroom stops, snacks, and leg stretches. Kids arrive fresh instead of fried. The silence of the electric motor means you can actually talk, play audiobooks, or let little ones nap without engine drone. And the cost savings — roughly 60% less than petrol — mean more budget for gudeg, batik, and temple tickets.

**Our advice:** Rent a BYD Atto 3 or Hyundai Ioniq 5 for comfort, download PLN Mobile and Charge+ before you leave, buy your e-Toll card with at least Rp 500,000 loaded, and give yourself 3-4 days. The Trans-Java Toll Road is Indonesia's first real EV highway — and it's ready for your family.

*Selamat jalan — happy driving!*

faq.question: Can I drive Jakarta to Yogyakarta without charging?
faq.answer: No — the distance is ~540 km and no current EV sold in Indonesia has that real-world range on a single charge. You'll need 2-3 charging stops depending on your EV's range. A BYD Atto 3 or Hyundai Ioniq 5 can do it with just 2 stops (about 30 minutes total charging time). A Wuling Air EV needs 4-5 stops plus overnight hotel charging.

faq.question: What's the best EV to rent for this trip in Indonesia?
faq.answer: For comfort, rent a BYD Atto 3 (420 km WLTP, Rp 600,000-900,000/day) or Hyundai Ioniq 5 (480 km WLTP, Rp 800,000-1,200,000/day). These have enough range for 2-stop trips and plenty of space for a family of 4. The Wuling Air EV (200 km WLTP, Rp 350,000-500,000/day) is the most common and cheapest rental but requires 4-5 charging stops and has limited luggage space.

faq.question: How much does the trip cost for a family of 4?
faq.answer: A one-way trip costs Rp 2,450,000-4,150,000 ($154-261 USD) on a budget or Rp 4,200,000-7,650,000 ($264-481 USD) mid-range for 3 nights including charging, tolls, hotels, meals, and activities. The EV charging itself is only Rp 200,000-350,000 ($13-22 USD) — roughly 60% less than the equivalent petrol cost.

faq.question: Are EV chargers reliable on the Trans-Java Toll Road?
faq.answer: Yes — reliability has improved significantly by 2026. PLN SPKLU stations at major rest areas have ~85% uptime. Newer Electrum (120 kW) and Charge+ (150 kW) stations report 90%+ uptime. Always check real-time availability on the PLN Mobile, Charge+, or Electrum apps before arriving. Carry a portable charger as a backup for emergencies.

faq.question: Can a family of 4 fit everything in a Wuling Air EV?
faq.answer: Barely. The Wuling Air EV is tiny — 4 adults fit but luggage is very limited (no real boot space). For a 3-4 day trip, you'd rely on backpack-style luggage or a roof box. We strongly recommend upgrading to a BYD Atto 3 for family comfort if your budget allows.

faq.question: What apps do I need for charging in Indonesia?
faq.answer: PLN Mobile (mandatory — find/pay at all PLN SPKLU stations), Charge+ (150 kW ultra-fast chargers along the route), Electrum (120 kW private network), Waze (real-time traffic), and PlugShare (community charger reports). Register and top up your wallet in all apps before departure — don't wait until you're at the charger.

faq.question: When is the best time to do this road trip?
faq.answer: The dry season (May-October) offers the best conditions — clear mountain views, less rain, and no flooding at rest areas. Avoid Lebaran (Eid al-Fitr, dates vary) when the entire Trans-Java corridor experiences mass exodus with gridlocked traffic and hour-long queues at charging stations.
